title: Three-trial grip curvature does not establish added walking-limitation prediction in a separate NHANES sample
abstract: In 1,237 NHANES 2013–14 adults aged ≥60 with complete bilateral grip tests and valid walking responses, adding normalized three-trial grip curvature to a frozen standard-strength model did not establish improved walking-limitation prediction: weighted Brier gain -0.0000785, approximate 95% interval -0.0018889 to 0.0010491. Source models were trained in 1,150 NHANES 2011–12 adults. Confirmation used a separate 2013–14 probability sample. Conventional strength summaries, demographics, asymmetry and linear trial change formed the baseline. Sensitivity estimates changed sign. Questionnaire equipment skips and complete bilateral testing limit scope; no equivalence or clinical utility is established.
